summary: M.S. Computer Engineering candidate at Rochester Institute of Technology (May 2026) with hands-on embedded firmware development across STM32 ARM microcontrollers and bare-metal C. Developed low-level I2C, UART, SPI, and GPIO drivers from scratch; debugged hardware interfaces using oscilloscopes and logic analyzers. Additional background in ROS2 robotics, FreeRTOS real-time systems, and PCB fabrication with real hardware deployment.

experience.title: General Secretary
bullets: Designed and fabricated custom single-layer PCBs in EAGLE for locomotive robots; implemented sensor communication over UART and I2C with closed-loop feedback.
Led a 25-member robotics team across national-level competitions, owning mechanical design, PCB fabrication, and AI/ML integration end-to-end.

experience.title: Embedded Systems Intern
bullets: Developed a wearable gesture-recognition glove integrating ADXL345 accelerometers with Raspberry Pi and HC-05 Bluetooth; translated 3-DoF hand motion into HID commands via Python.
Implemented a custom tap-detection algorithm using z-axis differential thresholding; resolved sensor jitter through software calibration and resolution tuning.

experience.title: Python Developer Intern
bullets: Developed a Python GUI using PyQt and Matplotlib for real-time data acquisition and experimental visualization in a laboratory environment.
Used GitLab for version control and collaborative technical documentation across a multi-team research environment.

projects.name: Object Tracking Turret
bullets: Used YOLOv8 on NVIDIA Jetson to detect and track objects, sending control commands to STM32 over UART.
Implemented multi-servo PWM control with interrupt-driven UART commands; used FreeRTOS with mutexes for shared-memory task coordination.
Integrated VL53L0X ToF sensing over I2C and OLED distance visualization.

projects.name: STM32 Bare-Metal Temperature Monitor
bullets: Built Cortex-M4 bare-metal C firmware for timer-synchronized temperature sensing with real-time display.
Implemented timer-triggered ADC scan conversions, interrupt-driven sample capture, and a low-level I2C driver.
Programmed GPIO, TIM2, ADC1, I2C1 in bare-metal C; achieved 3.68 KB Flash / 1.58 KB RAM at deterministic 1 Hz.

projects.name: Voice-Controlled Robotic Arm (COFFIN) — MS Capstone, RIT
bullets: Integrated dual VL53L0X ToF sensors via TCA9548A I2C mux for contact-aware grasping; two-link IK on Arduino in C++ for five-servo control.
Built a three-layer pipeline (Flutter → Flask-SocketIO → Jetson+Arduino); 100% pick reliability (10/10 trials) at ~11.5s end-to-end.
